name: Three-stage firing
summary: One firing in three stages turns a slip black and leaves the clay red. Air is let in, shut out, and let in again.
how: Fire the pot in an open kiln with air, so that the whole pot turns red.
Close the vents and add green wood, so that the whole pot turns black.
Open the vents and let the air in again at a lower heat.
Take out the pot: the fine slip stays black and the bare clay becomes red.

origin.note: Corinthian potters learn to make a black gloss and a red clay in one firing.

adoptions.via: Corinthian and Athenian painters draw black silhouettes in gloss slip, and the three stages fix the black.
Athenian painters keep the same firing and paint the background black instead of the figure.
